tests.notes: every possible key already exists with the value type's zero default; there is no way to distinguish 'never set' from 'explicitly set to zero'
mappings have no .length member -- there is no enumerable/countable notion of 'keys currently set'
mappings cannot be iterated; fails for the same root cause as 003 (no .length to drive a for-loop)
delete on a mapping key resets that key's value to the value type's zero default in place
mappings cannot be passed as function parameters at all, not even as an internal storage reference -- unlike storage struct references, which ARE allowed as parameters
public mapping getter takes the key as a parameter and returns the value, unlike a public scalar's zero-argument getter
mapping key types are restricted to elementary value types plus bytes/string; a dynamic array cannot be used as a key type
